objective: Require real two-way correlation between each map and the crawlable data it represents. A marker must control the matching page data and the matching page record must control the map, without false precision, unsafe condition claims, or search-surface proliferation.

baseline.note: Recalibrated after user testing of PR #77. The prior 95/100 benchmark rewarded the presence of insight copy and links but did not require stable data-key mapping or synchronized map/table state. Boat still correlated markers by DOM index and Shipwreck marker selection did not change the underlying table. This baseline reflects actual interaction value rather than string presence.

dimensions.note: Visible Boat hero remains a traceable real Michigan launch photograph. Five points remain lost because the old static/social fallback still exists in source HTML.

fatalPenalties: Boat marker-to-record correlation uses DOM/index position such as leaflet-interactive array order instead of a launch slug/key.
Boat filters change page records without changing the map marker set, or a page launch cannot focus/open its exact map marker.
A Shipwreck map marker only changes popup/insight copy while leaving unrelated table records visible.
A mappable Shipwreck table record has no reverse Show on map path to its regional anchor.
A shipwreck regional anchor is represented as an exact wreck, navigation, or dive coordinate.
A boat marker or NDBC regional observation is presented as ramp, harbor, or boating-safety truth.
Either parent canonical changes, thin child URLs are created, precise/personal location data is collected, or Circle Tour PR #51 is modified.
nextLossRemoval: Replace the Boat static root hero/og:image fallback with the same documented real photograph in a source-safe static media change. Do not weaken map-data correlation to remove this residual media loss.
